On conclusion of hearing today, the Supreme Court has permitted e-auction of the hotel building at 1, Mansingh Road, New Delhi. The copy of the final order is still awaited.The Supreme Court has also recorded that after conclusion of e-auction, while deciding the party to whom operating license of the hotel will be granted, NDMC will take into account the blemish less record of Taj, it's capabilities etc. Notably, IHCL will be entitled to participate in the e-auction. The Supreme Court has also directed that IHCL will continue to be in possession of the hotel till the e-auction and in the event the license to operate the hotel is granted to some other party, IHCL will be given at least six months to vacate the property."

The Company has now informed the Exchange vide their letter dated September 27, 2007, that: "At the Board Meeting held today, for approving the draft of the Offer document to be filed with SEBI, the Board of Directors decided to modify one of the two instruments comprising the Rights Issue. The modified Rights Issue proposals will now be as under. The company will make two simultaneous but unlinked Rights Issues as follows:- a) There will be no change in the Rights Issue of Equity shares to be offered to the shareholders in the ratio of 1:5 at a price of Rs.70 per share (of the face value of Rs.1 each). The price at which the Warrants would be exercisable and the specific period for exercising the Warrants will be fixed at the time of the actual issue. The NCDs with a maturity of 3 years would raise an amount of Rs.600 crores and a further sum of Rs.780 crores to Rs.900 crores (depending on the price to be fixed) would be raised when the Warrants are exercised. The increase in capital from this modified instrument would remain at Rs.6 crores as earlier proposed. Clarification of News : The media had reports that Indian Hotels Co. Limited may announce a bonus issue. The Exchange, in order to verify the accuracy or otherwise of the information reported in the media and to inform the market place so that the interest of the investors is safeguarded, had written to the officials of the company. Indian Hotels Co. Ltd. has vide its letter inter-alia stated, "The news item is not factual and is based on conjecture. No such proposal has been taken up by the Board of Directors of the Company".

Indian Hotels Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that the Company has entered into an agreement to purchase for Australian $ 36 million, the "W" Hotel located at 6 Cowper Wharf Road, Woolloomooloo, Sydney, currently owned by the Harilela Group of Hong Kong and managed by Starwood Pacific Hotels Pty Ltd under its "W" brand. Indian Hotels Co. Ltd. has informed the Exchange that at a meeting of the BOD's of the Company held on June 06, 2005, the BOD's have inter-alia recommended a dividend of 100% on Ordinary Shares of Rs.10/- each fully paid up of the Company (previous year 80% i.e. Rs.8.00 per Ordinary Equity Share of Rs.10/- each fully paid up). Accordingly : (i) the dividend payable on one Equity Share of Rs.10/- each fully paid up will amount to Rs.10/-; (ii) the dividend payable on 100 Equity Shares of Rs.10/- each fully paid up will amount to Rs.1000/-.
